key_insight: GIST-CMTF adds goal-state inference to causal tool filtering so LLM agents can avoid executing the right tool sequence for the wrong objective.
engineering_relevance: For tool-augmented agents, validating the intended goal before exposing actions can improve reliability while still keeping tool visibility minimal and token-efficient.
method: Predict candidate symbolic goals using the same state-transition vocabulary as CMTF.
Estimate goal ambiguity and either proceed with causal tool filtering or trigger clarification as a causal action.
Expose only the next causally necessary tool frontier once the goal state is sufficiently resolved.
evidence_signal: Across seven backends, six filtering methods, and 120 controlled tool-use tasks, GIST-CMTF reached 97.0% task success and reduced wrong-goal execution to 2.5% versus 19.4% for top-goal CMTF.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly inferring symbolic goal states, so ambiguous or underspecified requests may still require robust clarification handling and careful integration with downstream tool schemas.
paper_title: GIST-CMTF: Goal-State Inference for Causal Minimal Tool Filtering in LLM Agents
